I. IDENTIFY THE ZNF24–nTum-6.4314 GENOMIC ARCHITECTURE
======================================================

The ZNF24 chimeric architecture was identified in
*Myotis daubentonii*.

Two transcript configurations are associated with this locus.

The five-exon transcript contains four host-derived ZNF24 exons followed
by a terminal exon derived from the transposable element nTum-6.4314::

    ZNF24 exon 1
        |
    ZNF24 exon 2
        |
    ZNF24 exon 3
        |
    ZNF24 exon 4
        |
    nTum-6.4314-derived exon

A second transcript contains the same ZNF24 exons 1–3 and the same
nTum-6.4314-derived terminal exon but lacks ZNF24 exon 4::

    ZNF24 exon 1
        |
    ZNF24 exon 2
        |
    ZNF24 exon 3
        |
    nTum-6.4314-derived exon

Because these two transcripts can originate from the same genomic locus,
the comparative genomic analysis searches for the ZNF24–nTum-6.4314
locus rather than attempting to distinguish transcript isoforms.

ZNF24 exons 1–3 therefore constitute the shared host-gene anchor.
ZNF24 exon 4 is analyzed as an additional host-derived exon whose
presence can distinguish the longer genomic configuration, whereas
nTum-6.4314 is analyzed independently as the TE-derived component.


1. Create the ZNF24 analysis directory
---------------------------------------

Create an independent working directory

.. code-block:: bash

    cd /Volumes/Expansion/project3/bat_HTF_genomic_analysis

    mkdir -p ANALYSES/ZNF24/{intermediate,results,scripts,sequences}

    cd ANALYSES/ZNF24


2. Create the ZNF24 host exon probes
------------------------------------

The host probe set contains exons 1–4 from the five-exon
*Myotis daubentonii* transcript. Exons 1–3 are shared by both transcript
configurations.

Create the FASTA file

.. code-block:: bash

    nano sequences/ZNF24_host_exon_probes.fa

Use the following FASTA headers

.. code-block:: bash

    >ZNF24_exon1_match
    AGACAGGAAGCCGTCCGCGCCGGGGGCTTCTGGGAAACGGCTGAGAGCGGCGTCTCTGCGTCGGCCGCGGACAGCGAAGCCGCTGCGGTGCCCGAGCCCCAG

    >ZNF24_exon2_match
    

    >ZNF24_exon3_match
    GTCTCTCTCTGCCGGCGGAAGCGGGAGGTGCTGGTAGAGGAGATTGCATCTCAAGAAGAAGCGCAGGGATTACCGAGTTCGGAGCTCGATGCTGTGGAAAACCAGCTCAAGTGGGCGTCCTGGGAGCTCCACTCCCTCAGGCACTGCG

    >ZNF24_exon4_match
    

Paste the corresponding exon sequences supplied for the five-exon
*Myotis daubentonii* transcript.

Remove accidental whitespace

.. code-block:: bash

    sed -i '' '/^>/! s/[[:space:]]//g' \
    sequences/ZNF24_host_exon_probes.fa

Confirm the FASTA headers

.. code-block:: bash

    grep '^>' sequences/ZNF24_host_exon_probes.fa

The expected output is

.. code-block:: bash

    >ZNF24_exon1_match
    >ZNF24_exon2_match
    >ZNF24_exon3_match
    >ZNF24_exon4_match


3. Create the nTum-6.4314 TE-derived probe
------------------------------------------

The terminal TE-derived exon is identical between the two candidate
transcript configurations and is therefore analyzed independently.

Create the TE probe FASTA

.. code-block:: bash

    nano sequences/ZNF24_nTum-6.4314_probe.fa

Use the header

.. code-block:: bash

    >nTum-6.4314_match
    

Remove accidental whitespace

.. code-block:: bash

    sed -i '' '/^>/! s/[[:space:]]//g' \
    sequences/ZNF24_nTum-6.4314_probe.fa

Confirm the header

.. code-block:: bash

    head -1 sequences/ZNF24_nTum-6.4314_probe.fa

The expected output is

.. code-block:: bash

    >nTum-6.4314_match


4. Verify probe lengths
-----------------------

Verify that all host and TE probes were copied correctly

.. code-block:: bash

    awk '
    /^>/ {
        if (name) print name, length(seq)
        name=$0
        seq=""
        next
    }
    {
        seq=seq $0
    }
    END {
        print name, length(seq)
    }
    ' sequences/ZNF24_host_exon_probes.fa

    awk '
    /^>/ {
        if (name) print name, length(seq)
        name=$0
        seq=""
        next
    }
    {
        seq=seq $0
    }
    END {
        print name, length(seq)
    }
    ' sequences/ZNF24_nTum-6.4314_probe.fa


5. Validate the ZNF24–nTum-6.4314 locus in Myotis daubentonii
-------------------------------------------------------------

Use *Myotis daubentonii* as the positive reference species.

From the ZNF24 analysis directory

.. code-block:: bash

    cd /Volumes/Expansion/project3/bat_HTF_genomic_analysis/ANALYSES/ZNF24

Create the BLAST database directory

.. code-block:: bash

    mkdir -p intermediate/blast_db

Build a nucleotide BLAST database from the *Myotis daubentonii*
genome

.. code-block:: bash

    makeblastdb \
    -in ../../SPECIES/Myotis_daubentonii/*.fa \
    -dbtype nucl \
    -out intermediate/blast_db/Myotis_daubentonii

Search the four host-derived ZNF24 exons

.. code-block:: bash

    blastn \
    -query sequences/ZNF24_host_exon_probes.fa \
    -db intermediate/blast_db/Myotis_daubentonii \
    -task blastn \
    -word_size 7 \
    -dust no \
    -evalue 1e-10 \
    -outfmt '6 qseqid sseqid pident length qlen qstart qend sstart send evalue bitscore qcovhsp' \
    > intermediate/ZNF24_exon_matches_Myotis_daubentonii.tsv

Search the nTum-6.4314-derived exon independently

.. code-block:: bash

    blastn \
    -query sequences/ZNF24_nTum-6.4314_probe.fa \
    -db intermediate/blast_db/Myotis_daubentonii \
    -task blastn \
    -word_size 7 \
    -dust no \
    -evalue 1e-20 \
    -outfmt '6 qseqid sseqid pident length qlen qstart qend sstart send evalue bitscore qcovhsp' \
    > intermediate/ZNF24_nTum_matches_Myotis_daubentonii.tsv

Combine both searches

.. code-block:: bash

    cat \
    intermediate/ZNF24_exon_matches_Myotis_daubentonii.tsv \
    intermediate/ZNF24_nTum_matches_Myotis_daubentonii.tsv \
    > intermediate/ZNF24_all_matches_Myotis_daubentonii.tsv

Display the strongest matches for each probe

.. code-block:: bash

    sort -k1,1 -k11,11nr \
    intermediate/ZNF24_all_matches_Myotis_daubentonii.tsv \
    | awk '!seen[$1]++' \
    | column -t
